question: What conspicuity treatment is labeled 'E' in Figure 2A-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Item E in Figure 2A-1 is a "Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support." It is one of the permitted methods for enhancing the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign, applied here by extending a retroreflective strip down the sign post (shown ending within 2 ft maximum of the ground line). Options (permitted): - "Based upon engineering judgment, where the improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, any of the following methods may be used, as appropriate, to enhance the sign's conspicuity (see Figure 2A-1)" — the figure's Item E illustrates the vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support as one such method. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-1, Item E, shows a fluorescent yellow-green pedestrian crossing (W11-2) sign with diagonal downward arrow plaque mounted on a post that has a vertical fluorescent yellow-green retroreflective strip running down the sign support, with the strip ending "2 ft MAX." above the ground line. [Image 2] shows the same Figure 2A-1 in full-page context (page 48), with Item E labeled "Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support." Citations: - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49)
gold_answer: A vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support.
